title: Мужские принципы и встреча со знакомой  (Male Principles and Running into an Acquaintance)

segments.t: Viktor Petrovich explains to an offended Elena that he has never wanted to depend on a woman and that women have always moved into his place instead. Back at the apartment, Kostya warns Max that the Chef will never forgive him, while Nastya hands a menu to a bride-to-be who turns out to be her old friend Katya.
Ну да, это уважительная причина.
Лена, я не хочу зависеть от кого-нибудь.
Тем более от женщин.
Всегда переезжали ко мне.
Я же говорил, починил.
Сейчас я открою.
Шеф, а вам удобно сейчас говорить?
Все равно он тебя не простит.
О, а помнишь, когда ты с Викой поругался?
Да не, не вариант.
Доброе утро.
Ваше меню.
Офигеть, это ты?
Alright, let's go through it step by step in English.
Ну да, это уважительная причина.
'Oh sure, that is a very valid reason.' The grammar packs 'come on' and 'reason' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Лена, я не хочу зависеть от кого-нибудь.
'Lena, I do not want to depend on anyone.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'Lena' before landing on 'someone'.
Тем более от женщин.
'Especially not on a woman.' Elena brings out the contrast between 'that' and 'more' in a few short words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Всегда переезжали ко мне.
'Women have always moved in with me.' The meaning hinges on 'always' working together with 'for me' in spoken Russian.
Я же говорил, починил.
'I told you I fixed it.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'fixed' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Сейчас я открою.
'Hold on, I will get the door.' Elena anchors the line on 'any minute', while 'to open' completes the thought. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Шеф, а вам удобно сейчас говорить?
'Chef, is this a convenient time for you to talk?' The grammar packs 'chef' and 'to talk' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange.
Все равно он тебя не простит.
'He is not going to forgive you anyway.' The meaning hinges on 'all' working together with 'will forgive' in spoken Russian.
О, а помнишь, когда ты с Викой поругался?
'Oh, remember that time you had a huge fight with Vika?' Notice how Russian expresses 'about' and 'to quarrel' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Да не, не вариант.
'Nah, that is not an option.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'yes' and finishing on 'option'.
Доброе утро.
'Good morning to you.' Vika brings out the contrast between 'kind' and 'morning' in a few short words.
Ваше меню.
'Here is your menu.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'your' and finishing on 'menu'. Chef Viktor answers right away.
Офигеть, это ты?
'No way, is that really you?' Chef Viktor addresses the listener with the informal singular 'you' alongside 'you'. Alright, let's listen to all those lines again from the top.

Лена, я не хочу зависеть от кого-нибудь.
